subject: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end targets (hosted API vs current provider)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance requirements & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance SLOs and what we need to validate: 

Summary of Finlytics ask:
- Workload: real-time analytics augmentation (short completions, streaming token output to UI)
- Target throughput/concurrency: ~50 RPS sustained during business hours, spikes to ~200 RPS for 2-3 minute bursts
- Concurrency per-session: typical 2-4 parallel streaming sessions per user
- Streaming: yes — client expects token-level streaming to the browser with max end-to-end latency constraints
- p95/p99 end-to-end latency target (user-observed): p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 600 ms for the standard prompt/profile

Current provider (your notes): you mentioned measured p95 ~420 ms and p99 ~980 ms (includes network between app and provider endpoint). We discussed aiming for meaningful improvement if you migrate to Redwood hosted API or Redwood Dedicated.

What we need from you to run a short validation: 
1) Traffic profile: representative payload size distribution and token counts (small/medium/large) — if you can send the attached slo_matrix.xlsx with the profile filled that helps.
2) A test account / API key or a short window for us to run a load test against a staging endpoint (we can use your staging URL or spin up a controlled hosted test).
3) Clarify whether your p99 requirement is end-to-end from browser->app->provider->browser, or app->provider only.

Proposed next steps: 
- You send the traffic profile + confirm the measurement boundary (item 3) — Alex
- We run a two-hour synthetic load test (mix of streaming and non-streaming) and report p50/p95/p99 and tail traces — Redwood (Ben/Dev)
- Quick readout call to review results and recommend hosted vs Dedicated config (canary capacity, autoscale, caching) — schedule for next week if tests look good

Attachments: slo_matrix.xlsx (traffic profile template), prod-deployment-diagram.png (we'll annotate expected routing).

If the p99 target you listed (<=600 ms) is strict end-to-end, we should confirm network boundaries because our hosted API can typically achieve p95~150-250 ms and p99~300-450 ms for similar workloads depending on model and quantization. Dedicated pools can tighten those further with local networking. We'll validate with your traffic.

Thanks — available to jump on a 30-min test planning call Wed/Thu.

— Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Measurement boundary: when I said p95 ~420 / p99 ~980, that was measured app->provider->app (not browser network) using our internal synthetic harness. So the browser-to-app network adds a variable ~30-80ms depending on region. 
- Our strict requirement is p99 end-to-end (browser observed) <= 600 ms. If we take out average network overhead (50ms), that implies provider-side p99 target <= 550 ms. We listed 600ms as a ceiling to keep product integrity.
- Payload distribution: most requests are small — median request ~20 tokens out, 95th percentile ~120 tokens. Streaming is used for the top-level UI interactions where users expect immediate token-by-token UI updates.

I'll fill out slo_matrix.xlsx and upload by EOD. We can grant you access to our staging API key for a bounded window — I'll send a separate secure note to Dev with the staging URL and short-lived key.

Thanks — happy to schedule Wed 3/11 or Thu 3/12 for the readout after tests. Prefer Thu afternoon PST.

— Alex

Looping in a couple of quick engineering notes so expectations are set: 

- Hosted API baseline: for workloads like Alex describes (mostly small payloads, streaming enabled), our hosted API on a multi-tenant pool typically hits p95 140-220 ms and p99 300-420 ms end-to-end to the app in US-west regions (measured app->provider->app). Those numbers assume our standard tokenization and default batching.
- Dedicated option: reserved pools colocated with your app can reduce network jitter and get p95 down toward ~100-150 ms and p99 ~200-300 ms. This is with capacity sizing to meet sustained 50 RPS and burst headroom for 200 RPS.
- Streaming behavior: token-level streaming latency largely depends on batching window and model decode time. We can tune batching to favor latency (smaller batch windows) for the streaming endpoints you care about; tradeoff is higher cost per token.

Proposed technical plan: 
1) Use Finlytics staging key for a controlled 2-hour run (we'll run both streaming and non-streaming scenarios, with your supplied token-size distribution).
2) Instrument full-stack tracing (we'll provide an OpenTelemetry span mapping) so we can separate network overhead from provider processing time.
3) Deliver a short report with p50/p95/p99 and percentile breakdowns by request size + tail traces and configuration recommendations (hosted vs dedicated + batching/quantization knobs).

If Alex confirms the staging window, we can schedule the run Thu morning and a readout Thu 3/12 2:00 PM PST. That fits Marissa's proposed window.

— Ben
